description: No clean concept. Fires mostly in the opening (4-14 stones) when stones are piled in columns 2-3 (column 3 at least 2 high, column 2 at least 1), columns 0, 1 and 4 are empty or one high, and the opponent holds row 1-2 cells of columns 2-3. Opponent stones in column 0, at (1,1) or on column 4 switch it off.
effect: Small. Forcing it high raises column 3 by about 25-30 points and lowers column 4 by about 10-20 points. Zeroing it where it fires costs column 3 about 3-8 points.
program:
def _s(b):
    h = b.heights
    g = b.grid
    if b.ply > 14:
        return 0
    s = 0
    if h[3] >= 2: s += 1
    if h[2] >= 1: s += 1
    if h[4] <= 1: s += 1
    if h[1] <= 1: s += 1
    if h[0] == 0: s += 1
    o = sum(1 for (r, c) in [(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 2), (2, 3)] if g[r][c] == 2)
    if o >= 1: s += 1
    if o >= 2: s += 1
    return s

def fires(b):
    return _s(b) >= 6

def level(b):
    s = _s(b)
    return [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 7][s]
notes: 7 score calls. The best was the height-profile plus opponent-in-rows-1-2-of-columns-2-3 rule: F1 0.222 (P 0.17, R 0.31), AUROC 0.63, simulation share -0.08. Weighted cells, O-diagonal, enclosed-stone, bottom-row-alternation and 'poisoned column 4' ideas all scored F1 <= 0.18 or failed minimal pairs. Activation is highly conjunctive: it does not survive moving a pattern one column over, and far stones change it a lot (7.6 -> 0.3). Some late-game firing (a column among 1-3 left at about height 2) is not covered. Could be a random direction or a mixture.
